original_question: An isometric action of a group G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for every ε > 0 there exist R, N > 0 such that for every two points x, y with d(x, y) ⩾ R, there are at most N elements g ∈ G satisfying d(x, gx) ⩽ ε and d(y, gy) ⩽ ε. A group is said to be acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical action on a hyperbolic space with unbounded orbits. Is the automorphism group of a finitely generated acylindrically hyperbolic group also acylindrically hyperbolic?

refined_question: Let G be a finitely generated group. An isometric action of G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for every ε > 0 there exist R, N > 0 such that for every x, y ∈ S with d(x, y) ≥ R, there are at most N elements g ∈ G satisfying d(x, gx) ≤ ε and d(y, gy) ≤ ε. A group is called acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical action on a Gromov-hyperbolic metric space with unbounded orbits. If G is acylindrically hyperbolic, must its full automorphism group Aut(G) also be acylindrically hyperbolic? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
